questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a destination where I could experience the Spanish culture and learn the Spanish language. Moreover, I chose Madrid because of the opportunity to create relations to both national and international people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many aspects of my trip were great.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received most of the information when I arrived. There was a lot of trouble with my application and therefore, information about courses etc. were delayed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help from the international office from my faculty. Moreover, the university host many welcome sessions where they explain necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. I ended up reserving a room through
HousingAnywhere.com
, but the room ended up being a bad experience anyway. I recommend finding a room through the host institution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easier to get around the city with metro, and everything is more or less in walking distance. However, there is a lot of noise from the streets, from people, cars etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult to find, not a lot offered from the host institution.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Firstly, I had to register on their website, but since they did not receive my application in time, I had little time to do it and I did not have the necessary documents. Moreover, when you arrive you have to register again, and register to the courses again. Here you have to contact every professor and ask them if you can enroll in their classes and ask for them to sign a document. This took a lot of time, as some professors are really slow to answer, and you don't have much time to do so.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office is good to help with everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered to the classes I wanted at last. However, the first classes I wanted to take were not available to Erasmus students and I, therefore, had to find new courses to take when I arrived.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare everything and make sure you have all important documents beforehand. You can ask your exchange coordinator for help and ask them which documents you have to prepare.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were on the same level as UCPH but others are less.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH offers a lot of responsibility to your own teaching, whereas the Faculty of Information at UCM, takes on the responsibility to teach the students. This means that you have a lot of assignments, group work, classes, individual work, preparation to all, many exams, etc. It feels like being back in High School.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Tecnología de la Sociedad de la Información Aplicada a la Comunicación Audiovisual 
Sociología 
Arte Español Contemporáneo 
Marketing Aplicado a los Medios Audiovisuales 
Historia del Cine

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Arte Español Contemporáneo (Publicidad y Relaciones Públicas). Great teacher, and exciting work projects. We had a lot about how art can help selling a product, and how this can be done. Moreover, the most important times in art history, and important tools to analyze an art piece.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I expected to buy many books, but it was not necessary, as they had the books in the library or online.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can join sport teams and activities, visit museums for free with UCM and go to events in the libraries.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit the museums because of the cultural aspects, and also very instructive.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to other Spanish cities. City Life Madrid offers many weekend and week trips to other cities or to other nearby countries, very cheap. Go to the parks (ex. Retiro Park). You can also do yoga or sports for free in the parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy because i was prepared.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Write in WhatsApp groups and ask if any wants to go out for a coffee or a drink. Ask your fellow students to go out as well. Go to meetups etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of costumer service, especially with my booking agency.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Free tapas, helpful people, and that Madrid is a safe place.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare your registration and prepare your courses beforehand, check which courses are available to Erasmus students. 
2. Meet a lot of people and go on trips on the holidays, and go to the events organized by the institution. 
3. Ask for help, the international office, the teachers and the students are good at helping with everything.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning the language, student exchange, getting to know national and international people, and experience the culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Registration, finding a place to live, keep up with the workflow and still being social.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
